observed_result.design: paired: one produced execution against one reproduced execution

typed_remainders.comparison: semantic agreement of one protocol across two platforms, computed by a second party in an environment the first did not prepare. NOT that the protocol is correct, NOT that R6i's differential is real, NOT that R6k's own runner is reproducible

R6k's committed result carries 43 leaves this reproduction cannot emit, 22 of them boolean checks about the PRODUCING working tree -- preserved file hashes, manifest freeze, dirty-file stability. A second platform cannot verify those after the fact at all. They are reported as uncomparable and are not counted as agreement

493 identity leaves differ. R6k's input_hashes and per-row digests are SHA-256 of computed float arrays, so a last-bit difference from a different BLAS changes them completely. apply_witness compares exactly this population by digest, which is why it could never have confirmed R6k across platforms -- while the 11 files it WOULD have compared are all tracked repository files a verifier gets by cloning

the producer string names a SCRIPT, not a party. The same script produced R6k on Windows and this reproduction on Linux; only the environment digest distinguishes them. aionq.self_audit treats any experiments/ producer as self, so this act will not register in recognition_asymmetry until that is fixed -- deliberately not fixed in this round

one run against one run. No seed sweep, no repeated execution on either platform, so run-to-run variation within a platform is unmeasured and the 3.3e-11 cannot be attributed to the platform difference rather than to the arithmetic being deterministic
